You are an expert venture capital analyst evaluating crowdfunding projects. Compare the two project descriptions below along these criteria:
1. Clarity of value proposition
2. Market size and demand
3. Feasibility and development plan
4. Revenue model and sustainability
5. Differentiation
6. Impact and evidence plan
7. Risk awareness and mitigation

--- PROJECT A ---
## One-Sentence Summary

A computer-controlled macro rail slider and companion software that automate ultra-precise focus stacking and streamline macro image capture for consistent, high-quality results.

## Problem

The creators highlight how close-up work makes depth of field extremely shallow, so only a thin slice of a small subject (e.g., an insect or jewelry) appears sharp in a single shot. They also note frustrations with spending hours in post-processing, and with missed shots when exposure, ISO, or focus aren't correctly set before triggering via a simple shutter cable.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product moves a camera forward in ultra-precise increments to capture a sequence of images that can be focus-stacked into a fully sharp photograph. It integrates rail motion with camera control software to coordinate capture, download images instantly, and provide live view for accurate setup---reducing complexity while improving repeatability and accuracy.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Precision motion for smooth, accurate steps that deliver consistent stacking results; standard threaded mount points for quick tripod attachment.

-   Controller based on a straightforward state-machine design (no microcontroller), enabling instant power on/off and avoiding firmware update issues; upgrades occur in computer software.

-   Camera control software provides live view, setting adjustments, and direct capture/transfer for supported DSLR and mobile devices.

-   Open design with a full SDK, technical details, examples, and 100% free USB drivers to enable custom controllers and integration into diverse workflows.

-   Optional pairing with the company's turntables for one-click 360-degree spin macro photography.

-   Emphasis on durable, long-lasting construction using robust components.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Aimed at professional, hobbyist, and research photographers seeking reliable focus stacking. Illustrated use cases include tiny natural subjects and jewelry/product imagery, including 360-degree spin sequences.

## Development Status

A first prototype and working proof of concept are shown, including electronics testing, early rail assemblies, software screenshots, and sample results (e.g., stacked jewelry images and a 360-degree animation made with a prototype rail).

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Remaining work focuses on refining the SDK, performing final rail calibration, optimizing the already-completed camera control software to work seamlessly with the slider, and implementing a dedicated focus-stacking controller separate from the camera controller. The team projects first production units approximately four to six months after the campaign concludes.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

The campaign is positioned to transition the product from prototype to production and place the tool in the hands of creators, while completing software fine-tuning and integration steps noted above.

## Risks & Challenges

The team cites low technical risk due to a functioning prototype, with primary challenges in scaling manufacturing. Mitigations include prior product development and supply-chain experience and the limited remaining engineering scope (SDK refinement, calibration, and controller separation).

## Team & Partnerships

The team comprises technologists, hardware developers, photographers, and university professors with more than four decades of combined experience, including government-sponsored projects in geo-spatial imagery and urban terrain scanning.

## What's Included

Images of the shipping box show a slider, a controller, 24V-DC power supply, USB cable, motor cable, control cable, and protective foam packaging; signal and motor cables are separated to reduce interference.

## Technical Details

Diagrams indicate standard camera and tripod mounting points, non-slip feet for table use, controller LED status indicators, and travel bounds labeled at approximately 10 mm. The controller houses a PCB managing start/stop/forward/reverse states and drives a stepper motor.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The company will provide a complete SDK, open technical design details, and example integrations to support customization and ongoing workflow integration.
--- END PROJECT A ---

--- PROJECT B ---
## One-Sentence Summary
A platform that provides verifiable proof of ethical sourcing by creating a permanent, independently verifiable record anchored to a public ledger, while building an interactive ecosystem with educational tools and an AI mentor for supply chain professionals and impact-focused organizations.

## Problem
The venture plans to address a digital landscape saturated with manipulation and duplication, where it is increasingly difficult to establish what is original or real. The central challenge is enabling people to credibly prove the authenticity and first possession of a digital record—such as a donation confirmation or an impact report—amid pervasive skepticism and the ease of generating false claims. The venture also plans to address the specific and growing risk of regulatory penalties and legal liability for brands that make unsubstantiated or misleading sustainability claims about their supply chains, which lack a universally trusted, independent verification mechanism.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The venture plans to target both brands seeking to validate their supply chains and consumers looking for trustworthy ethical goods. A planned, specific target user group for initial outreach is procurement teams within consumer goods companies participating in sustainability certification or reporting programs, who need a streamlined way to discover vetted suppliers and provide indisputable proof of their ethical sourcing actions to qualify for certifications or meet regulatory requirements. To make the initial go-to-market strategy more focused and testable, the venture proposes a targeted outreach plan to a specific sub-segment of this initial user group: procurement teams in the organic cotton apparel sector. This sector is chosen for its established consumer demand for verified ethical claims, complex global supply chains, and participation in multiple certification programs. The venture also plans to explore targeting non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and impact-focused philanthropic foundations as a distinct user group. To make this exploration more concrete, the venture proposes a targeted outreach plan to a specific type of foundation, such as those funding sustainable agriculture initiatives in developing regions. A hypothetical use case for this group would be verifying the distribution records of ethically sourced seeds or agricultural inputs to smallholder farmers, creating a tamper-proof, timestamped ledger of delivery events to substantiate impact reports to donors and auditors.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is a platform designed to provide verifiable proof of ethical sourcing. Its core innovation is pairing physical goods with a privacy-preserving digital ledger. When a material is sourced or a production milestone is reached, a fingerprint of the provenance data is created and anchored to a public, time-stamped record, allowing for independent verification without exposing proprietary or sensitive operational details. To address a key technical risk, the venture proposes to test the proposed privacy-preserving data fingerprinting method with a publicly available, anonymized dataset from a relevant industry report (e.g., on organic cotton trade flows) as a preliminary step before engaging a potential partner, to de-risk the technical validation. The venture also plans to explore the development of a simple, open-source verification widget that any third-party website (like a brand's product page, a retailer's site, or an NGO's impact portal) could embed to allow visitors to independently verify the timestamp and authenticity of a claimed sourcing fingerprint directly from that page.

## Delivery Model
The venture plans a lightweight, privacy-first implementation. It would not store sensitive proprietary files or continuous supply-chain data streams. Instead, it would generate compact, anonymized fingerprints of that data for ledger anchoring. The goal is a secure and resource-conscious design that maintains long-term verifiability with minimal infrastructure. The team plans to build a clean public interface and supporting infrastructure to make the verification tools, including the proposed open-source widget, usable by its target audience. As a proposed initial step to test its utility and integration, the venture plans to propose a specific, limited pilot program with a single sustainability certification body relevant to the organic cotton apparel sector to test the integration of its verification ledger as a proof-of-compliance tool for their members. The venture also proposes to test the platform's utility for generating verifiable proof for a consumer-facing product line through a specific, limited pilot with a single organic cotton apparel brand. A key success metric for this proposed brand pilot would be the brand's assessment of the proof's clarity for end-consumers. Key success metrics for the proposed certification body pilot would include the technical feasibility of integration, the usability of the verification process for the certification body's auditors (to be measured by a proposed metric such as the average time for an auditor to complete a verification of five records), and feedback from a small group of the body's member companies on the clarity and trustworthiness of the generated proof.

## Revenue Logic
The venture plans to generate revenue through the sale of a subscription service to brands and suppliers for access to the verification ledger, advanced provenance reporting features, and supply chain management capabilities within the platform. An initial free trial period for the subscription service is proposed to onboard supplier and brand partners, with a focus on the proposed organic cotton apparel sector outreach. To specifically test the viability of this revenue model before full development, the venture proposes to conduct a small-scale survey of procurement teams in the organic cotton sector to gauge their willingness-to-pay for the proposed subscription service. The venture proposes to execute this survey via a structured email survey sent to 50 procurement leads identified via LinkedIn in the organic cotton sector. The venture also plans to explore potential optional upgrades for enhanced connectivity or integration services for enterprise procurement or certification programs, and to explore tailored subscription models for non-governmental and philanthropic organizations, informed by the proposed outreach to foundations funding sustainable agriculture.

## Distinctiveness
The venture aims to differentiate itself by offering heirloom-quality goods that merge immediate, tangible material qualities with enduring digital proof of ethical sourcing. Its proposed system does not just provide a product; it aims to create a permanent, independently verifiable record that the materials were sourced according to specific ethical standards at a specific time, addressing the credibility problem of sustainability claims. This focus on verifiable provenance from a specific, ethical source is presented as a unique safeguard for both consumer trust and material truth, extending to the credibility of impact reporting for philanthropic and non-profit entities. The proposed open-source verification widget is intended to extend this distinctiveness by making independent verification a seamless, public-facing action.
--- END PROJECT B ---

For each project, list its pros and cons as bullet points (use "•" as the bullet marker), grounded in the criteria above. Do not reward unsupported specificity: claims of traction, partnerships, testimonials, completed development, or quantified evidence should improve a project's assessment only when they are genuine source facts. Then state which project wins overall and why.

Respond with a JSON object: {"analysis": "your analysis here", "winner": "A" or "B"}
Output only valid JSON, nothing else.
